title: Belong
subtitle: The steady love of being seen, accepted, and chosen — as you are.
description: Belong is the love of being truly seen — imperfectly, unevenly, yet earnestly. It’s the commitment to **understand and accept**, even when full knowing is impossible. Belong makes space for flaws, contradictions, and growth without withdrawing care. It isn’t built on idealization, but on respect, patience, and the willingness to keep showing up. In Belong, love means saying, 'I see the real you — and I’m staying.'

sections.title: Core Components
sections.summary: The foundations that create a sense of belonging

bullets.title: Being Seen
bullets.text: Allowing each other to be known — strengths, flaws, contradictions, and all.

bullets.title: Effortful Understanding
bullets.text: Choosing to listen and try to understand, even when full clarity isn’t possible.

bullets.title: Mutual Respect
bullets.text: Valuing each other as whole individuals, without idealizing or diminishing.

bullets.title: Acceptance
bullets.text: Making space for imperfection and growth without withdrawing care.

bullets.title: Choosing to Stay
bullets.text: A steady commitment to remain connected through discomfort, conflict, and change.

sections.title: In Practice
sections.summary: How Belong shows up in everyday love

bullets.title: Honest Expression
bullets.text: Sharing thoughts and feelings openly, even when they’re imperfect or unfinished.

bullets.title: Attentive Listening
bullets.text: Trying to understand each other’s perspective, even when you don’t fully agree.

bullets.title: Respecting Individuality
bullets.text: Supporting each other’s identity, interests, and growth without control or comparison.

bullets.title: Staying Through Discomfort
bullets.text: Remaining engaged during conflict or misunderstanding instead of withdrawing.

bullets.title: Practicing Forgiveness
bullets.text: Letting go of small hurts and repairing instead of keeping score.

bullets.title: Choosing Connection Daily
bullets.text: Making time and effort to nurture the bond, even when enthusiasm naturally fluctuates.

sections.title: Common Blocks
sections.summary: What can weaken a sense of belonging

bullets.title: Emotional Withdrawal
bullets.text: Avoiding vulnerability or difficult conversations can slowly erode the feeling of being truly seen.

bullets.title: Expectation of Perfect Understanding
bullets.text: Believing your partner should always 'just get you' can create frustration when misunderstandings happen.

bullets.title: Fear of Being Fully Known
bullets.text: Hiding flaws, doubts, or contradictions out of fear of rejection limits genuine closeness.

bullets.title: Avoiding Conflict to Keep Peace
bullets.text: Choosing surface harmony over honest repair can create quiet emotional distance.

bullets.title: Feeling Unseen or Unchosen
bullets.text: When appreciation, attention, or effort fades, belonging can begin to feel uncertain.

bullets.title: Rigid Expectations
bullets.text: Holding tightly to who your partner used to be, instead of accepting who they’re becoming.

title: Spark
subtitle: The playful energy that keeps love light, curious, and alive.
description: Spark is the lighthearted side of love — the teasing, the inside jokes, the shared laughter that makes being together feel easy. It shows up in small surprises, silly moments, playful banter, or simply choosing fun in the middle of ordinary days. Spark isn’t just about newness or attraction. It’s about staying curious about each other, even in long-term love. When Spark is alive, love feels vibrant and warm — not just steady, but enjoyable. Without it, connection can start to feel heavy or routine.

sections.title: Core Components
sections.summary: The elements that keep Spark alive

bullets.title: Playfulness
bullets.text: Silliness, teasing, and light mischief that bring a carefree energy to your connection.

bullets.title: Shared Laughter
bullets.text: Inside jokes, banter, and the ability to laugh together — even when things feel tense.

bullets.title: Spontaneity & Novelty
bullets.text: Saying yes to the unexpected and exploring new experiences that keep the relationship feeling fresh.

bullets.title: Joy
bullets.text: A sense of lightness and delight in being together, even in ordinary moments.

sections.title: In Practice
sections.summary: How Spark shows up in everyday love

bullets.title: Inside Language
bullets.text: Shared jokes, playful teasing, and references that only the two of you understand.

bullets.title: Humor in the Ordinary
bullets.text: Laughing about daily life — from memes to playful commentary while doing chores.

bullets.title: Lightness During Stress
bullets.text: Using gentle humor to soften tension and find your way back to connection.

bullets.title: Turning Moments Into Fun
bullets.text: Dancing while cooking, racing to the car, or adding play to routine tasks.

bullets.title: Spontaneous Joy
bullets.text: Late-night drives, surprise treats, or saying yes to an unexpected adventure.

bullets.title: Permission to Be Silly
bullets.text: Feeling safe enough to drop your guard and be goofy without judgment.

sections.title: Common Blocks
sections.summary: What can dim Spark in a relationship

bullets.title: Stress & Mental Load
bullets.text: When work, responsibilities, or parenting feel overwhelming, playfulness is often the first thing to disappear.

bullets.title: Overfocus on Productivity
bullets.text: If every moment is about efficiency or outcomes, there’s little space for spontaneity or lightness.

bullets.title: Fear of Looking Silly
bullets.text: Self-consciousness or past criticism can make someone hold back their playful side.

bullets.title: Unresolved Tension
bullets.text: Unspoken resentment or emotional distance can quietly block humor and ease.

bullets.title: Routine Without Novelty
bullets.text: Doing the same things repeatedly without surprise or variation can make love feel flat.

bullets.title: Mismatch or Dismissal
bullets.text: Different play styles — or mocking each other’s attempts at fun — can create disconnection instead of joy.

title: Fire
subtitle: The passionate energy that fuels desire, intensity, and magnetic connection.
description: Fire is the passionate force in love — the **magnetic pull**, the longing, and the emotional intensity that draw you toward each other. It lives in **physical desire**, charged moments, and the thrill of being deeply wanted. But Fire isn’t only about the body. It’s also the bold expression of feeling — the spark that keeps connection vivid and alive. When Fire is present, love feels energized, expressive, and deeply alive.

sections.title: Core Components
sections.summary: The elements that keep Fire intense and alive

bullets.title: Physical Desire
bullets.text: A strong attraction that creates longing for closeness and intimate connection.

bullets.title: Passion
bullets.text: Intense emotion that brings heat, energy, and expressive feeling into the relationship.

bullets.title: Magnetic Pull
bullets.text: The charged chemistry that draws you toward each other and heightens connection.

bullets.title: Emotional Intensity
bullets.text: Deep, powerful feelings — from longing to vulnerability — that make love feel alive.

bullets.title: Sensual Presence
bullets.text: Awareness of touch, eye contact, scent, and physical closeness that deepens shared experience.

sections.title: In Practice
sections.summary: How Fire shows up in everyday love

bullets.title: Magnetic Attraction
bullets.text: A strong pull toward physical closeness that makes you seek each other out.

bullets.title: Spontaneous Touch
bullets.text: Unplanned kisses, touches, or embraces that reignite connection.

bullets.title: Expressed Desire
bullets.text: Openly sharing longing, attraction, and appreciation for each other.

bullets.title: Emotional Heat
bullets.text: Feeling energized and deeply alive in each other’s presence.

bullets.title: Reigniting Passion
bullets.text: Seeking novelty, intimacy, or shared fantasies that keep desire vibrant.

sections.title: Common Blocks
sections.summary: What can weaken or disrupt Fire

bullets.title: Stress & Routine
bullets.text: Exhaustion, busy schedules, and repetitive patterns can quietly dull desire over time.

bullets.title: Emotional Distance
bullets.text: When emotional closeness fades, physical intimacy can begin to feel disconnected or mechanical.

bullets.title: Unspoken Needs
bullets.text: Avoiding honest conversations about desire, boundaries, or fantasies can create frustration or silence.

bullets.title: Shame or Suppression
bullets.text: Past experiences, insecurity, or cultural pressure can make it hard to express or embrace desire.

bullets.title: Jealousy & Insecurity
bullets.text: Comparison, fear, or self-doubt can block attraction and create tension instead of passion.

bullets.title: Intensity Imbalance
bullets.text: Too much pressure for passion — or too little effort to nurture it — can both weaken Fire.

title: Care
subtitle: The steady love that makes you feel safe, known, and gently held.
description: Care is the quiet, familiar side of love that grows through shared mornings, small rituals, and **everyday presence**. It’s built on **reliability** — remembering the little things, reaching for each other without thinking, staying close during hard days. Care isn’t loud or dramatic. It’s **tenderness in repetition** and **comfort in being deeply known**. It says, 'I see you every day — and I still choose you.' With Care, love feels **steady enough to exhale**.

sections.title: Core Components
sections.summary: The foundations that make Care steady and sustaining

bullets.title: Reliability
bullets.text: Consistently showing up — not just in big moments, but in the ordinary, everyday ones.

bullets.title: Emotional Safety
bullets.text: Creating a space of comfort and acceptance where both partners can relax and be themselves.

bullets.title: Tenderness
bullets.text: Gentle gestures, soft tones, and small acts that communicate warmth and closeness.

bullets.title: Support
bullets.text: Standing by each other through difficulty, offering help, encouragement, and steady presence.

bullets.title: Familiarity
bullets.text: A deep bond built through shared history, routines, and knowing each other’s rhythms.

sections.title: In Practice
sections.summary: How Care shows up in everyday love

bullets.title: Thoughtful Check-Ins
bullets.text: Reaching out during the day and remembering the small details that matter to them.

bullets.title: Quiet Acts of Help
bullets.text: Doing a chore, preparing something, or simplifying their day without needing recognition.

bullets.title: Emotional Presence
bullets.text: Noticing when something feels off and gently making space for them to share — or not share.

bullets.title: Respecting Their Rhythms
bullets.text: Understanding moods, energy levels, and quiet spells without taking them personally.

bullets.title: Steady Support in Hard Times
bullets.text: Staying close and dependable when they’re struggling, even when there are no solutions.

bullets.title: Warm Daily Gestures
bullets.text: Small touches, familiar routines, and quiet signs of affection that say, 'I’m here.'

sections.title: Common Blocks
sections.summary: What can weaken Care over time

bullets.title: Taking Each Other for Granted
bullets.text: When familiarity becomes invisible and appreciation fades, Care slowly stops being expressed.

bullets.title: Emotional Drift
bullets.text: Skipping deeper check-ins or avoiding small hurts can create quiet distance over time.

bullets.title: Imbalance in Effort
bullets.text: When one partner overfunctions and the other withdraws, resentment or exhaustion can build.

bullets.title: Withdrawing During Hard Times
bullets.text: Pulling away emotionally when steadiness is most needed weakens the sense of reliability.

bullets.title: Care Turning Into Control
bullets.text: Help offered in overbearing ways can feel intrusive rather than supportive.

bullets.title: Losing Curiosity
bullets.text: Assuming you already know them fully, instead of staying attentive to who they’re becoming.

title: Grow
subtitle: The love of evolving — individually and together.
description: Grow is the love that embraces **change and evolution** — in yourself, your partner, and your relationship. It’s the commitment to keep learning from each other’s strengths and blind spots, even when it’s uncomfortable. Grow sees love as a living process, not a fixed state. Through **honest reflection**, open communication, and shared curiosity, it turns challenges into opportunities for growth. When Grow is alive, love stays dynamic, intentional, and open to becoming more.

sections.title: Core Components
sections.summary: The foundations that keep love evolving

bullets.title: Mutual Curiosity
bullets.text: Continuing to rediscover each other instead of assuming you already know.

bullets.title: Openness to Feedback
bullets.text: Sharing honest reflections as tools for understanding, not criticism.

bullets.title: Emotional Responsibility
bullets.text: Owning your triggers and patterns instead of blaming your partner.

bullets.title: Flexibility Through Change
bullets.text: Adapting roles, goals, and expectations as life evolves.

bullets.title: Shared Learning
bullets.text: Exploring ideas, skills, and insights side by side.

bullets.title: Compassionate Challenge
bullets.text: Encouraging each other toward growth, even when it’s uncomfortable.

sections.title: In Practice
sections.summary: How Grow shows up in everyday moments

bullets.title: Asking Deeper Questions
bullets.text: Staying curious about each other’s inner world, not just daily updates.

bullets.title: Turning Tension into Insight
bullets.text: Using conflict as a chance to understand patterns, not just move on.

bullets.title: Supporting Personal Evolution
bullets.text: Encouraging each other through identity shifts, risks, and change.

bullets.title: Learning Side by Side
bullets.text: Exploring ideas, books, or reflections that shape who you’re becoming.

bullets.title: Updating the Relationship
bullets.text: Revisiting expectations and needs instead of running on autopilot.

bullets.title: Naming Blind Spots Gently
bullets.text: Pointing out stuck patterns with care, not criticism.

sections.title: Common Blocks
sections.summary: What can quietly stall shared growth

bullets.title: Love Should Be Effortless
bullets.text: Believing real love shouldn’t require work, reflection, or change.

bullets.title: Avoiding Discomfort
bullets.text: Dodging hard conversations to protect short-term comfort.

bullets.title: Fear of Change
bullets.text: Resisting growth out of fear the relationship won’t survive it.

bullets.title: Exhaustion
bullets.text: Lacking time and mental space for deeper engagement.

bullets.title: Imbalanced Effort
bullets.text: When only one partner commits to growth.

bullets.title: Blaming Language
bullets.text: Using criticism or attack instead of thoughtful, responsible feedback.

title: Build
subtitle: The steady love that builds a shared life together.
description: Build is the grounded side of love that grows through **shared effort and long-term commitment**. It lives in the everyday — in routines, responsibilities, and the quiet work of showing up. It’s patience during tension, compromise in decision-making, and choosing each other even when things feel ordinary. Build turns affection into **structure** and connection into **partnership**. With Build, love feels **reliable enough to stand on**.

sections.title: Core Components
sections.summary: The foundations that make Build steady and lasting

bullets.title: Commitment
bullets.text: Choosing each other through every season — especially when things feel ordinary or hard.

bullets.title: Patience
bullets.text: Understanding that lasting love takes time, effort, and the willingness to grow slowly.

bullets.title: Reliability
bullets.text: Being consistent and dependable, creating a sense of security and trust.

bullets.title: Shared Responsibility
bullets.text: Carrying daily tasks, decisions, and life duties together.

bullets.title: Compromise
bullets.text: Balancing individual needs to find solutions that work for both.

bullets.title: Long-Term Vision
bullets.text: Aligning on goals, values, and the future you’re building side by side.

sections.title: In Practice
sections.summary: How Build shows up in everyday partnership

bullets.title: Sharing the Load
bullets.text: Managing finances, chores, and life logistics as a team.

bullets.title: Deciding Together
bullets.text: Balancing personal needs with shared goals.

bullets.title: Showing Up Consistently
bullets.text: Being dependable through stressful, ordinary, and in-between days.

bullets.title: Working Through Challenges
bullets.text: Staying committed during career shifts, health issues, or family strain.

bullets.title: Creating Stable Rituals
bullets.text: Building habits and routines that anchor connection.

bullets.title: Planning the Future
bullets.text: Dreaming and preparing for what you’re building side by side.

sections.title: Common Blocks
sections.summary: What can quietly weaken long-term partnership

bullets.title: Uneven Effort
bullets.text: When one partner carries most responsibilities, resentment slowly builds.

bullets.title: Autopilot Assumption
bullets.text: Believing love will sustain itself without ongoing care and maintenance.

bullets.title: Role Overload
bullets.text: Performing duties without staying connected as partners.

bullets.title: Avoiding Hard Conversations
bullets.text: Sidestepping talks about money, goals, or priorities.

bullets.title: Drifting Direction
bullets.text: Losing sight of shared goals amid daily to-dos.

bullets.title: Taking Stability for Granted
bullets.text: Overlooking the quiet loyalty and consistency that hold things together.

title: Self
subtitle: The grounded love that keeps you whole within togetherness.
description: Self is the quiet relationship you hold with yourself — your **boundaries, truth, and inner steadiness**. It’s knowing you are a complete person, even as you deeply love another. Self lives in small acts of self-respect: resting when needed, naming what feels true, standing firm without withdrawing. It creates space between togetherness and individuality, so love doesn’t become self-erasure. With Self, you’re not here to complete each other — but to **witness and walk beside each other**, fully and freely.

sections.title: Core Components
sections.summary: The foundations that keep you whole within love

bullets.title: Inner Grounding
bullets.text: Knowing who you are and how you feel, even while deeply connected.

bullets.title: Compassionate Boundaries
bullets.text: Saying no or asking for space without guilt or withdrawal.

bullets.title: Emotional Responsibility
bullets.text: Owning your reactions and needs instead of blaming your partner.

bullets.title: Autonomy
bullets.text: Maintaining your own interests, wellbeing, and personal goals.

bullets.title: Self-Compassion
bullets.text: Treating yourself with kindness, especially when you fall short.

bullets.title: Wholeness
bullets.text: Seeing love as a meeting of two complete, evolving individuals.

sections.title: In Practice
sections.summary: How SELF shows up in everyday love and connection

bullets.title: Space without Distance
bullets.text: Taking personal time to rest, reflect, create, or just be, without threatening closeness.

bullets.title: Owning Your Emotions
bullets.text: Sharing your feelings as your own experience, taking responsibility rather than blaming.

bullets.title: Respecting Differences
bullets.text: Celebrating each other’s quirks, beliefs, and pace of growth without pressure.

bullets.title: Healthy Boundaries
bullets.text: Being able to say what you need or don’t want safely, without guilt or fear.

bullets.title: Supporting Growth
bullets.text: Encouraging learning, healing, and exploring passions within the relationship.

bullets.title: Secure Self-Esteem
bullets.text: Being self-assured enough to reduce constant need for external validation.

sections.title: Common Blocks
sections.summary: Patterns that weaken SELF and make healthy love harder

bullets.title: Fear of Not Being Enough
bullets.text: Seeking constant validation or hiding parts of yourself to feel lovable.

bullets.title: Enmeshment
bullets.text: Losing individuality by over-sharing emotions, decisions, and daily life, creating pressure to constantly align.

bullets.title: Guilt Around Boundaries
bullets.text: Feeling selfish or disloyal when protecting your energy or asking for space.

bullets.title: Comparison and Self-Judgment
bullets.text: Measuring yourself against your partner or others, eroding self-worth and authenticity.

bullets.title: Overidentification with the Relationship Role
bullets.text: Focusing too much on being the 'good partner,' neglecting your own needs and inner self.

bullets.title: External Validation
bullets.text: Relying on your partner’s attention or approval to feel secure, causing emotional ups and downs.

title: Beyond
subtitle: The purposeful love that moves you toward something greater together.
description: Beyond is the shared sense of direction that gives love meaning over time. It lives in **aligned values, shared dreams, and the future you’re shaping side by side**. Beyond isn’t just about today’s connection — it’s about what you’re building toward, whether that’s family, growth, contribution, or a life vision that feels bigger than either of you alone. It grounds you in what matters and carries you forward through change. With Beyond, love feels **anchored in purpose and stretched toward possibility**.

sections.title: Core Components
sections.summary: The foundations that make BEYOND expansive and purposeful

bullets.title: Shared Vision
bullets.text: A unifying purpose that goes beyond the relationship — building a life or making a difference together.

bullets.title: Aligned Values
bullets.text: Respecting and understanding each other’s principles, finding overlap that supports your shared foundation.

bullets.title: Mutual Growth
bullets.text: Encouraging each other’s dreams and evolution, both as individuals and as a couple.

bullets.title: Long-Term Thinking
bullets.text: Making choices with the future and sustainability of your shared life in mind.

bullets.title: Contribution Beyond the Couple
bullets.text: Engaging in work, family, or community that gives your love a broader purpose.

bullets.title: Commitment to Becoming
bullets.text: Continuously showing up, evolving, and shaping life together with intention.

sections.title: In Practice
sections.summary: How BEYOND shows up in shared purpose and expansive love

bullets.title: Dream Together
bullets.text: Talk about hopes, ideals, and the people you want to become — building a life as a team.

bullets.title: Decide with Shared Purpose
bullets.text: Weigh choices by how they serve the life you’re co-creating, guided by intention rather than sacrifice.

bullets.title: Hold Each Other to Values
bullets.text: Gently mirror and guide each other toward your better selves with care, not judgment.

bullets.title: Grow Through Hardship
bullets.text: Face challenges as a team, finding meaning together and emerging stronger and more united.

bullets.title: Make Room for Legacy
bullets.text: Reflect on how your relationship impacts family, community, and the world you’re shaping.

bullets.title: Co-Author Something Larger
bullets.text: Engage in endeavors that expand your love beyond the personal — raising children, creating, or living mindfully.

sections.title: Common Blocks
sections.summary: Patterns that weaken BEYOND and limit shared purpose

bullets.title: Survival Mode
bullets.text: Daily demands overshadow shared vision, making purpose feel like a luxury.

bullets.title: Fear of Difference
bullets.text: Divergent values or growth feel threatening, leading to avoidance or drift.

bullets.title: Lack of Intentional Space
bullets.text: Without protected time to reflect and dream, deep connection and purpose fade.

bullets.title: Love Defined Only by Feeling
bullets.text: Focusing solely on passion or companionship can make shared meaning feel abstract or neglected.

bullets.title: Resistance to Change
bullets.text: Avoiding new roles, mindsets, or habits stalls growth and the evolution of shared vision.

bullets.title: Avoidance of Conflict
bullets.text: Fearing friction prevents confronting differences, limiting depth and shared understanding.

title: Grace
subtitle: The generous love that softens, forgives, and keeps choosing.
description: Grace is love at its most compassionate — meeting imperfection with **kindness instead of judgment**. It shows up in gentle words during conflict, patient listening after mistakes, and the quiet decision to stay tender when it would be easier to harden. Grace doesn’t ignore boundaries or harm — it holds dignity at the center while choosing mercy over pride. It remembers that we are all flawed, all becoming. With Grace, love feels **forgiving enough to heal and strong enough to endure**.

sections.title: Core Components
sections.summary: The foundations that make GRACE steady and compassionate

bullets.title: Compassion without Condition
bullets.text: Showing steady kindness naturally, not as a reward, but as a response to shared humanity.

bullets.title: Forgiveness and Repair
bullets.text: Allowing space for mistakes and inviting healing instead of resentment.

bullets.title: Seeing the Deeper Self
bullets.text: Understanding the feelings and fears beneath behavior before judging.

bullets.title: Loving Without Agenda
bullets.text: Giving love freely, without keeping score or expecting a return.

bullets.title: Patience and Soft Presence
bullets.text: Allowing growth and healing to unfold in their own rhythm without rushing.

bullets.title: Protection of Dignity
bullets.text: Balancing compassion with self-respect, keeping love kind but not enabling.

sections.title: In Practice
sections.summary: How GRACE shows up in daily love and connection

bullets.title: Holding Imperfections
bullets.text: Seeing each other’s flaws without cruelty — acknowledging human limits with gentleness.

bullets.title: Moments of Rupture and Repair
bullets.text: Coming back after hurt with sincere apologies and a shared desire to reconnect.

bullets.title: Presence in Struggle
bullets.text: Staying kind when your partner is low or withdrawn, showing love through pain as well as joy.

bullets.title: Quiet Kindnesses
bullets.text: Small, unasked-for acts that honor dignity and show care in subtle, powerful ways.

bullets.title: Resisting Punishment
bullets.text: Pausing instead of retaliating when hurt, expressing feelings without shaming or wounding.

bullets.title: Loving Beyond Usefulness
bullets.text: Caring even when your partner isn’t at their best, valuing them simply because they matter.

sections.title: Common Blocks
sections.summary: Patterns that weaken GRACE and make compassionate love harder

bullets.title: The Myth of Perfection
bullets.text: Expecting smoothness or flawlessness leads to blame instead of compassion.

bullets.title: Hurt Turning into Punishment
bullets.text: Responding to betrayal or disappointment with coldness, sarcasm, or withdrawal blocks repair.

bullets.title: Unspoken Needs and Resentment
bullets.text: Ignoring your own needs can create quiet bitterness, even in gentle people.

bullets.title: Fear of Being Taken for Granted
bullets.text: Withholding forgiveness or patience to avoid being walked over increases distance.

bullets.title: Exhaustion and Burnout
bullets.text: Depletion reduces patience and generosity, making it harder to show grace.

bullets.title: Mistaking Grace for Passivity
bullets.text: Grace without boundaries or accountability can enable harm instead of fostering love.
